Aaron Donald’s return to the NFL has unexpectedly reopened an old chapter in Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s relationship. As Donald credited his wife, Erica, for helping him make the difficult decision to return, NFL insider Clarence Hill Jr. drew a pointed comparison to Brady’s own comeback and the concerns that surrounded his marriage to Bündchen.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen were married in 2009 and built one of the NFL’s most closely watched power couples. So when Brady announced his retirement in 2022, his decision appeared to signal a new phase for their family.Brady said at the time that he wanted to devote more attention to his wife and children. But his retirement lasted only 40 days. He soon reversed course and confirmed that he would return for another season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.Bündchen supported Brady publicly, but the situation was reportedly more complicated behind the scenes. As the season progressed, reports suggested that the quarterback’s return had created tension in their marriage. Bündchen also spoke about her concerns over Brady continuing to play, particularly as the demands of professional football remained a major part of his life.The couple ultimately announced their divorce in October 2022.That history resurfaced after Erica Donald joked about her husband’s own return to football. Her playful message suggested that she had given Aaron Donald the green light to leave home and resume his NFL career.Hill responded with a short but loaded comment:"If only had Gizelle had been equally supportive"The remark quickly shifted attention away from Donald and back toward Brady and Bündchen.Aaron Donald’s situation has one major difference. The Rams star has openly credited his wife with playing a major role in his decision to return.Speaking to reporters after agreeing to a one-year, $20 million contract with Los Angeles, Donald explained how much his family’s approval mattered."I think my wife played a huge part in this, me making this decision, period," Donald said. "Because, if the wife wasn't happy, it wasn't gonna get done. We gotta make sure that the household was good. The kid was okay with it all, having them hard conversations, figuring things out. What I wanted to do, if I was gonna do it, how would we do it."So, my wife was onboard. She said, 'If you wanna do this, just put your 100%.' ... She played a huge part in me figuring this out because it really wasn't an easy decision."Donald’s comments offer a striking contrast to the circumstances surrounding Brady’s comeback. Rather than simply celebrating a return to football, he stressed the conversations that took place at home before making his choice.That distinction is what gave Hill’s comment its edge. His comparison does not change the reality of Brady and Bündchen’s relationship, but it has revived public interest in one of the most talked-about moments of their marriage.For Brady, the decision to return ultimately marked the beginning of a difficult period in his personal life. For Donald, his comeback is arriving with his wife’s backing and a clear understanding of what the move means for his family.

Article Title: When did Novak Djokovic marry wife Jelena? All about their wedding and love story
Article Text:
When did Novak Djokovic marry wife Jelena? All about their wedding and love story

Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic married days after his Wimbledon win

Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic’s relationship began in high school

Novak Djokovic married his longtime girlfriend Jelena Ristic on July 10, 2014, in Montenegro, just four days after winning his second Wimbledon title. The couple held their civil wedding at the Aman Sveti Stefan resort on the Adriatic coast, while a private church ceremony followed on July 12. Jelena was pregnant with their first child at the time. The wedding came after years of a relationship that began when the two met as teenagers in Belgrade and later stayed together despite long periods apart. Their son Stefan was born three months later, followed by daughter Tara in 2017.The timing made July 2014 especially memorable for Novak Djokovic. On July 6, he defeated Roger Federer in a five-set Wimbledon final and lifted his second title at the tournament. During his celebration, Djokovic dedicated the win to his future wife and their unborn child.“I would like to dedicate it to my future wife and our future baby,” Djokovic said after the victory. “I’m going to become a father soon and I’m still preparing for that. It’s a great joy in life.”Four days later, he and Jelena exchanged vows at Aman Sveti Stefan in Montenegro. The civil ceremony was followed by a church wedding on July 12 at the Church of Saint Stephen, with the second ceremony kept private for close family.Jelena wore an ivory wedding dress designed by Sarah Burton for Alexander McQueen. Djokovic later spoke about seeing her for the first time as his bride, describing the moment in emotional terms.“Seeing her for the first time in her wedding dress, smiling and walking towards me… She looked like an angel,” Djokovic told Hello! magazine. “I was focused on her, and her smile and our baby. It really was a perfect moment.”The wedding came as the couple prepared for a major change in their lives. Their son Stefan was born in October 2014, only a few months after they became husband and wife.The story of Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic goes back much further than their wedding day. They first met during their high school years in Belgrade and began their relationship in 2005.Their early years were not always easy. Jelena studied at Bocconi University in Milan while Djokovic was building his tennis career, leaving them to manage a long-distance relationship. Jelena later explained how difficult travel was for them when they were younger.“I was a student barely getting by, and he was a very young tennis player who also had no money to spare on expensive trips,” she has explained. “Airplanes were, at the time, something utterly out of our reach. We contrived and devised these plans how to meet, how to make our relationship work.”Djokovic proposed to Jelena in September 2013, after the couple had spent years together. Their engagement was publicly confirmed that month, with Djokovic sharing his happiness about calling Jelena his future wife.By the time they married, their relationship had already lasted for nearly a decade. Djokovic later told People, “She’s the only serious relationship I ever had. She’s been my girlfriend, fiancée and my wife for more than 20 years, and I’m eternally grateful for her love, her support, the relationship that has evolved over the years.”Jelena has also remained closely involved in the Novak Djokovic Foundation, where she serves as global CEO. The foundation focuses on early childhood education and preschool development in Serbia. The couple have since raised two children, Stefan and Tara, while Jelena has continued to support Novak both personally and through their shared work.
Article Summary: Novak djokovic married his longtime girlfriend jelena ristic on july 10, 2014, in montenegro. The wedding came just four days after he won his second wimbledon title. The couple met as teenagers in belgrade and began their relationship in 2005.

Jimmy Butler injury update news is heating up again, and for once it comes with something concrete attached to it. The Golden State forward has been sidelined since tearing his ACL midway through the 2025-26 season, and for months there was no real clarity on when he'd suit up again.A fresh report suggests Butler could be closer to a return than most expected, arriving just as his name keeps surfacing in trade conversations around the league. Here's what's being said, and why his next few months matter for Golden State's plans.Jimmy Butler, 36, tore his ACL in the middle of the Warriors' 2025-26 season, and for a long stretch afterward there was no specific date attached to his recovery, just the general assumption he'd get back on the floor for Golden State at some point this year.Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints reported that Christmas Day is emerging as the earliest realistic target for Butler's return, though he stressed nothing is locked in yet. Siegel said there have been small but encouraging signs in Butler's rehab and floated that he could even be ahead of the typical ACL recovery curve. On his Clutch Scoops podcast, he said, "I fully anticipate him being back before the trade deadline."Siegel also offered a wider window in a separate piece, pointing to January or February 2027 as the more conservative estimate, with the exact date depending on how Butler progresses and what the Warriors' medical staff decides once the season gets underway. Golden State itself hasn't put out any official update on his recovery.Even with a return timeline is on the horizon, Butler's long-term future in the Bay Area is a little skeptical.Siegel has suggested that if Golden State is struggling and sitting near the bottom of the Western Conference by the deadline, a sell off becomes likely, with Butler, in the final year of his contract, among the pieces most likely to be moved. Other players around Stephen Curry could follow, all in service of stockpiling assets ahead of a bigger swing in 2027.The Warriors could still pull off a major trade without touching Butler, but he is their most valuable trade piece if the front office decides to chase another star. Adding to the uncertainty, Butler, Curry, and Draymond Green are all entering the final year of their deals together, which makes the 2026-27 season a genuine crossroads for the franchise.Before the injury, Butler was putting up strong numbers across 38 games, averaging 20.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.9 assists while shooting 51.9 percent from the field and 37.6 percent from three.Butler is currently in the second and final year of that extension, which he signed after declining his previous player option. Once it expires, he'll hit unrestricted free agency, and that expiring money is exactly why his name keeps surfacing in trade talk. A large expiring salary is often the simplest way to make the money work on a bigger deal.For now, health is the more immediate concern. If Butler really is trending toward a Christmas return, the Warriors get their two-way problem solver back right as playoff positioning starts to matter, and any trade decision gets a lot easier to make with him healthy on the floor instead of just a name on paper.

Christmas day is emerging as the earliest realistic target for butler's return, though he stressed nothing is locked in yet.

Article Title: GOATbye: Leo blows whistle on Messimerising international career
Article Text:
File Pic - Argentina's Lionel Messi kisses the trophy after winning the World Cup in 2022. (AP/PTI Photo)

Lionel Messi in numbers

Lionel Messi in numbers

Lionel Messi for Argentina

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It was morning in Miami and late evening in India as Lionel Messi’s announcement through an Instagram post flooded social media. Having seen him light up our lives for two decades, the world suddenly felt strangely empty, unfamiliar. His great rival Cristiano Ronaldo must feel so lonely today.“After all this time since the (2026 World Cup) final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone I’m retiring from the national team…”The post showed three handwritten pages in Spanish, in which the Argentina captain confirmed he is retiring from the Albiceleste.As a footnote, he added: “I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I am even more convinced than before.”Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, died on Aug 8 at a hospital in the central Argentine city of Rosario. He was 68.“It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment.”Messi is 39, and after two decades of watching him adorn the hallowed blue-and-white striped shirt, many will lament his decision to go, but no one can question it.Having lit up six World Cups, winning the tournament in Qatar 2022 and leading Argentina to the final in 2014 and 2026 — an incredible journey from wunderkind to the champion elder of the beautiful game — he held the world in a thrall.For over a decade, modern football was defined by the transcendent rivalry between Messi and the Portugal superstar Cristiano, an era-defining battle that eclipsed clubs, countries, and competitions. It was unbelievable theatre. It had to end someday.Even in a life as hallowed as his, such a difficult call needs a real breaking point. Exactly 10 years ago, after the 2016 Copa America final loss to Chile, Messi had called it a day, frustrated at the world, Argentina’s cursed fortunes and, somewhat unbelievably, in doubt about his abilities.An outpouring of concern from his team, earnest pleas from countrymen — and the rest of the world — forced a reversal.His words then were telling.“A lot of things went through my mind on the night of the final and I gave serious thought to quitting, but my love for my country and this shirt is too great. We need to fix many things in Argentinian football, but I prefer to do this from inside and not criticise from outside.”Things didn’t change immediately, though. Argentina’s World Cup debacle in Russia 2018, with Messi further cutting a lonely, isolated figure, as Luka Modric first, and then Mbappe, then only 18, tore through his team, only reinforced the sinking feeling that it was not to be.Slowly, though, it changed. New coach, old teammate Lionel Scaloni structured the team around him, gave him the freedom, appreciation and confidence he needed. All this, with a band of adoring, talented players around him.What followed was a monumental Copa America triumph — beating Neymar’s Brazil 1-0 at the famed Maracana, the same venue where he first lost a final in 2014 — marking his first major international trophy.Qatar would prove his high noon, a series of dazzling, often otherworldly performances that would earn him the World Cup winner’s medal that he so richly deserved and that had eluded him for so long. It sanctified his seat in the pantheon.This summer, in America, too, the highest-scoring man in South American football history led Argentina to the final before a young Spain proved insurmountable.Messi calls time as his country’s all-time leading goal scorer and most capped player.In 2016, Messi’s first announcement had sprung from the failures on the pitch and repeated questions on his loyalty to Argentina. But he just chipped away to finally turn things on their head. The heartbreak of the 2014 Maracana final and a string of continental disappointments had weighed heavily on him.In 2016, after blasting his penalty over the bar in the Copa America Centenario final against Chile, his call to quit international football was emotional and abrupt.“I tried so hard to be champion with Argentina. I couldn’t do it,” Messi had rued.But Argentina wasn’t ready to let him go. “No te vayas” — don’t go — became the weeping cry of a nation desperate to hold on to him.Messi gave himself a second chance.From being a prisoner of ‘dependencia’ — Argentina’s dependence on him — to the bearer of the proverbial cross, Messi’s ‘back nine’ expedition was sprinkled with trophies.Usually reticent, unwilling to pour out his heart, Messi redefined himself in his last World Cup. After scoring his first World Cup hat-trick against Algeria and launching Argentina’s title defence, Messi opened up.“Everything I’m experiencing now is a bonus. I’ve been fortunate enough to achieve all my dreams — or even more than I ever dreamed of achieving — both professionally and personally.”Two months down the line and a bereavement must have precipitated that lack of meaning and motivation. Not like the prince of Denmark, who sought revenge to restore order in a distorted world, though. More akin to calm of mind, all passion spent.Of course the universe of football will be asking for more, but Messi’s personal loss, perhaps, asked for a realignment. Argentina must learn to live with it.
Article Summary: Lionel messi has announced he is retiring from the argentina national team. The 39-year-old made the announcement through an instagram post. Messi’s father, jorge messi, died on aug 8 at a hospital in the central argentine city of rosario. Messi gave himself a second chance.

Lionel Messi’s decision to end his international career has prompted an emotional reaction across Argentina, with President Javier Milei among those paying tribute to the captain who delivered some of the greatest moments in the country’s football history.Messi announced on Monday that he had decided to retire from international football following a period of reflection after Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The decision brought an end to a remarkable international career spanning six World Cups, 207 appearances and 125 goals for his country.Argentina President Javier Milei was among the first prominent figures to respond to Messi’s announcement.Sharing a photograph of the forward greeting supporters on Instagram, Milei wrote: “Muchas gracias HOMBRE IMPOSIBLE...!!!”The message roughly translates to: “Thank you very much, impossible man.”Milei’s tribute reflected the significance of Messi’s contribution to Argentine football, particularly after the forward helped end years of disappointment with the national team.Messi’s announcement came more than a month after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium on July 19, a result that left the 39-year-old with another World Cup final defeat to add to his international story.The decision also arrived just weeks after Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, died on August 8 in Rosario at the age of 68, adding another deeply personal dimension to an already difficult period for the Argentina captain.Messi confirmed his international retirement through an emotional statement on Instagram, explaining that he had reached the point where he felt he had nothing more to give while also acknowledging the emergence of a younger generation within the national team.“After all this time since the final match, and after long reflection, I want to announce to everyone that I have decided to retire from playing with the national team,” Messi said.“It was a painful decision and it still hurts me deep down, but I realise that the time has come.”The Argentina captain stressed that his commitment to the national team had never wavered throughout his career, including during the years when major international success repeatedly eluded him.“I swear to you that I always gave everything I had, not only during the recent years in which we achieved everything, but before that too, and I always fought and gave all I had for this shirt, and to make you happy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” he added.Messi also acknowledged that the arrival of younger players had helped convince him that the time was right to step aside.“I have exhausted everything I have, and I no longer have any more to give, alongside the presence of a group of wonderful young players who deserve to get their chance,” he said.Messi’s relationship with the Argentina national team was not always defined by the success that eventually came towards the end of his career.The forward suffered several major disappointments with his country, including defeat to Germany in the 2014 World Cup final and losses in consecutive Copa América finals before finally winning his first major senior international trophy at the 2021 Copa América.That triumph ended Argentina’s 28-year wait for a major international title and marked the beginning of an extraordinary period for Messi and his country.A year later, Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a thrilling final finished 3-3 following extra time.Messi scored twice in that final and converted his penalty during the shootout, helping Argentina win the World Cup for the first time in 36 years and the third time in the country's history.He then helped Argentina retain the Copa América in 2024 before leading the team to another World Cup final in 2026, where Spain ultimately denied them back-to-back titles.Despite that final defeat, Messi leaves international football having achieved almost everything available to him with Argentina, including the World Cup, two Copa América titles and Olympic gold.Messi's longevity at international level is perhaps best illustrated by the fact that he appeared at six different World Cups between 2006 and 2026.Across those tournaments, he scored 21 goals in 34 appearances, placing him second on the all-time World Cup scoring list behind France captain Kylian Mbappé, who has moved ahead of him with 22 goals.Messi had previously overtaken Germany legend Miroslav Klose's tally before Mbappé eventually claimed the record.The 2026 tournament was another productive campaign for Messi individually, with the Argentina captain scoring eight goals and providing four assists.His performances included his first World Cup hat-trick, which came against Algeria during the tournament, further adding to a collection of records that had grown throughout his international career.By the time he announced his retirement, Messi had also established himself as Argentina's most-capped player and leading goalscorer, with 207 appearances and 125 goals according to the figures accompanying his retirement announcement.He also finishes as the highest-scoring player in South American international football.Although his international career is over, Messi has not announced his retirement from club football and will continue playing for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.The Argentine remains a central figure for the American club and underlined that status in spectacular fashion on August 30, scoring four goals and providing an assist for Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes 92, becomes youngest batter to hit Duleep Trophy fifty
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi plays a shot during the Duleep Trophy Semi-final (PTI Photo)

Tilak hits patient ton

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: In 118 minutes and 81 balls, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi offered a glimpse of the raw talent that has made him one of Indian cricket’s most sought-after prospects. The southpaw backs his big-hitting ability irrespective of the format and his fearless approach was on full display as the East Zone opener smashed 92 (7x4, 7x6) against Central Zone on Day 2 of their Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Monday.At 15 years and 157 days, Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a 50 in the tournament, breaking Central Zone’s Laxman Singh’s record of 16 years and 23 days, set way back in Jan 1969.The innings was more than just a record. Since his Ranji Trophy debut in 2024, the teenager had managed 215 runs from nine first-class matches. While he has built strong credentials in white-ball cricket, the longer format remains a stern test. Sooryavanshi was in no mood to let a red-ball challenge pass without making a statement.The first session was all about his attacking display. After getting off the mark with a risky single, the left-hander struck his first boundary with a stylish square drive. That was merely an appetiser, as he repeatedly looked to score in the ‘V’ against the pacers, including Yash Thakur , whom he deposited over the bowler’s head for his first six.His 18 singles were as much a sign of maturity as his seven sixes were of his power. His domination helped East Zone race to 64 in the first 10 overs. On 40, Sooryavanshi was handed a reprieve when Yash Rathod dropped a straightforward catch off Saransh Jain. The batter made the most of it, bringing up his half-century off 42 balls with a six over long-on.However, he was left distraught when another attempt at a maximum landed in Arshad Khan’s hands at deep mid-wicket off Harsh Dubey, leaving him eight runs short of his maiden first-class hundred. Along with Abhimanyu Easwaran’s 69, Sooryavanshi’s 92 formed the backbone of a 161-run opening stand that helped East Zone reach 266, exactly matching Central Zone’s first-innings total. Central were 45/3 at stumps.In the longer format, patience and discipline are traditional routes to building an innings. The beauty lies in embracing that challenge when the situation demands it.South Zone found themselves in that situation. At 80/5, they were staring at the prospect of conceding a first-innings lead to North Zone, who had posted 195. What followed over the next 271 minutes was an exhibition of restraint and disciplined batsmanship as Tilak Varma (106 batting, 225b, 7x4) and Shreyas Gopal (87, 169b, 11x4) took centre stage with a 175-run sixth-wicket partnership.Their stand turned the tide, helping South secure a first-innings lead. They were 285/9 at stumps, 90 ahead.Brief scores: Central Zone 266 & 45/3 (M Kumar 2-14) vs East Zone 266 all out ( V Sooryavanshi 92, A Easwaran 69; H Dubey 4-66); North Zone 195 vs South Zone 285/9 in 94 overs (o/n: 40/2) (Ti Varma 106*, S Gopal 87; G Brar 4-70).
Article Summary: At 15 years and 157 days, sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a 50 in the tournament. His domination helped east zone race to 64 in the first 10 overs. Tilak varma (106 batting, 225b, 7x4) and shreyas gopal (87) took centre stage with a 175-run sixth-wicket partnership.

Article Title: Mariano Navone went from watching Novak Djokovic win his 1st Grand Slam in 2008 to sending his idol home in his 1st-round exit in 2 decades: From Challenger grind to ‘La Navoneta’
Article Text:
Mariano Navone

From spending weekends at the club to the biggest stage

The rise of ‘ La Navoneta ’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Mariano Navone walked into Arthur Ashe Stadium as the lesser-known name, a 25-year-old Argentine facing one of the biggest names tennis has ever produced. He walked out with the biggest victory of his career; and, perhaps most remarkably, having beaten the player he once watched and idolised.Navone stunned Novak Djokovic in the first round of the US Open on Sunday, winning 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in a marathon that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. Djokovic, the 24-time Grand Slam champion, was battling physical problems and frustration, but Navone refused to be intimidated by the occasion or his opponent.The Argentine kept coming even after Djokovic took control by winning the second and third sets. By the fourth, Djokovic was visibly struggling, while Navone sensed an opportunity and seized it. He eventually became the first player to beat Djokovic in the opening round of the US Open and handed the Serbian his earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades.For Navone, though, the significance went beyond the scoreboard.“(It) was very tough for me because you are playing with the ‘GOAT’ on this court,” Navone said, recalling the surreal experience of facing his childhood idol. “For sure it's the best thing I've had on court. This is an amazing court and the biggest stage. It's amazing, the way we play. I mean, five sets. ... I'm very happy. I don't know. What can I say?”And then came the simplest description of what the night meant to him: “It's unbelievable.This means a lot. It's a dream come true.”Navone's relationship with tennis began long before the bright lights of New York. He picked up a racket at a local club in Argentina when he was just three years old. Tennis was not something that entered his life from the outside, it was already woven into his family.“I learned with a coach. My sister, mother, and father all play tennis. They love tennis,” Navone said in a 2023 interview.The club quickly became almost a second home. His uncle, family members and friends were regular opponents, and Navone spent much of his childhood there.“I played a lot of matches at the club with my uncle, family, friends. All the time, I went to the club. At seven or eight, I would spend five or six hours all the weekends. I was there all the time when I was kid!”That early immersion helped shape the player he would eventually become: competitive, resilient and comfortable grinding through long matches.His rise, however, was far from overnight.Before breaking into the world's top 100, Navone spent years working his way through the ATP Challenger circuit. By 2023, he had won five Challenger titles, all coming in the previous year. Those tournaments became the foundation of his professional career and, as he explained, changed his outlook on the sport.“Challengers have changed my life,” he said. “I made my first final in 2022 in Corrientes. In that moment, I was around 520 in the rankings. The level of Challengers has given me everything. The matches have a lot of intensity. The competition, the players are so special. They've developed my game and mentality. It's a challenge all the time to win matches. It's very difficult to win.”Navone's breakthrough arrived at the Rio Open in 2023. He entered the ATP 500 event without a single tour-level victory and left it as one of the week's biggest stories.He had previously gone 0-2 at tour level, losing in the first round at Cordoba and then Buenos Aires. Rio changed everything.Starting through qualifying, Navone defeated Federico Coria, Yannick Hanfmann, Joao Fonseca and defending champion Cameron Norrie to reach the final. He became only the 11th qualifier to reach an ATP 500 final since the series began in 2009.His run also sent him soaring up the rankings. From No. 113, he was set to break into the world's top 100 for the first time and could have climbed as high as No. 40 with the title.There was another part of Navone's growing identity that fans were beginning to embrace. It was his nickname, "La Navoneta"."La Navoneta" is a playful reference to "La Scaloneta", the nickname associated with Argentina's national football team manager Lionel Scaloni.“La Navoneta is like the same, but with less people because I'm not very famous!” Navone said. “The people represent me with that because I have charisma, so I think the people represent me with that name. The people don't say, 'Mariano', they say 'La Navoneta’!”The nickname suited a player whose rise had become a story of momentum, persistence and belief.Yet there was another Argentine influence in his tennis. Navone grew up admiring David Nalbandian, particularly the former world No. 3's backhand. He called Nalbandian a very good player and person.But above all, there was Djokovic.Navone's admiration for the Serbian began when he was a child watching Grand Slam tennis. He remembers seeing Djokovic win his first Australian Open title in 2008 and immediately recognising something special.“I saw him at Roland Garros, because I played my first Grand Slam [last] year and I said, 'Wow!' I am a fan of Djokovic, I think he's the best player I've seen on the court. When I saw him win his first Grand Slam at the 2008 Australian Open, I was like, 'Wow, this guy is very special!' and what a career, right?”Years later, the boy who watched Djokovic from afar stood across the net from him at the biggest tournament of his life.And this time, it was Navone who made the memory, by sending his idol home.
Article Summary: Mariano navone beat novak djokovic 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2. 6-1 in a marathon that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. Navone picked up a racket at a local club in argentina when he was just three years old. Tennis was not something that entered his life from the outside. Argentine reached atp 500 final for the first time in his career.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend andre agassi said he gave up his childhood to have his children's childhood. The quote is closely connected to agassi's own experience growing up. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life. Andre agassi and steffi graf have two children, jaden and jaz.
